findings.title: Non-string dtype objects equal to supported names bypass refusal
findings.reproduction: probe_edges.py accepts collections.UserString("float32") in all five entries. nonstring_random_review.py reaches data conversion in tensor and advances the real NumPy RNG in randn/rand; the C++ boundary is intercepted, so no device call occurs.
findings.argument: Set/dict membership tests equality and hash, not isinstance(dtype, str). The _np_dtype docstring and review require every non-string to be refused before conversion/allocation/random draws.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate isinstance(dtype, str) before the _DEVICE_CAST_DTYPE membership test in both tensor and make, with the registered TypeError; add non-string tests including UserString and unhashable objects.
findings.status: open; fix outside review write scope

findings.title: L38 accepts an unrelated failure containing the registered TypeError text
findings.reproduction: python3 artifacts/eng2/rev1/probe_edges.py: wrapped_other_reason and wrong_type_exact_text return reasons=[] for a pinned ID with exception_class=AssertionError. A plain unrelated AssertionError is correctly refused.
findings.argument: The pin branch checks a substring in the complete pytest longrepr, without checking the terminal exception class/message. Quoted text in another failure is sufficient.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the call-phase terminal exception to be TypeError with the registered exact message, using structured exception data; reject other exception classes and extra failures. Add the constructed negative cases.
findings.status: open; fix outside review write scope

findings.title: All registered mutant killer IDs fail the matcher
findings.reproduction: python3 artifacts/eng2/rev1/probe_edges.py: all 15 mutants have self_matching=0 across all registered killers.
findings.argument: matches() strips tensor_cuda/tests/test_eng2.py:: from the observed ID but compares it to registry patterns retaining that prefix. evaluate() therefore reports no registered killer ID failed even when a real registered killer fails and executes the mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize both observed IDs and registered patterns consistently, preserving literal parameter brackets; verify every registered killer self-matches and exercise a real CPU MF1/MF2 receipt through evaluate().
findings.status: open; fix outside review write scope

findings.title: Cross-arm byte scoring compares unnormalized arm-specific test IDs
findings.reproduction: python3 artifacts/eng2/rev1/cross_arm_review.py: collect 262 real IDs per arm, call the actual _record with identical constructed hashes, then execute the unchanged scoring loop. Both f1bytes (35/35 rows) and p302bits (20/20 rows) report IDs equal False and every baseline row differing.
findings.argument: test_eng2.py:57 stores request.node.nodeid, including artifacts/eng2/tool/arms/baseline or candidate. score_gpu.py:46-47 keys by that raw string, so no corresponding row can match.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize row test_id with evidence.norm_id on both sides before comparing, reject duplicate normalized IDs, and verify the expected 35/20 row census. Keep hashes unchanged.
findings.status: open; fix outside review write scope

findings.title: The all-entry dtype census omits Python entries and a residual private fallback
findings.reproduction: python3 artifacts/eng2/rev1/census_review.py: functional._causal_mask(0,0,"cpu",dtype) returns float32 for float64, double, int32, not_a_dtype and None. Three quantization.affine scale_dtype/out_dtype entries are also absent from L60 JSON; they use NumPy conversion semantics.
findings.argument: The existing 201 rows reproduce, but are not an exhaustive census of tensor_cuda/tensor_cuda. The ledger mentions the private mask assumption without emitting its required per-input rows. Its callers currently pass Tensor.dtype, so unsupported-name reachability is limited to direct private calls.
findings.suggested_fix: Complete the census with the omitted Python entries and their baseline outcomes. Guard the private mask against unsupported/non-string dtype arguments before constructing a tensor, or obtain an explicit scope exception for that internal-only contract; preserve valid NumPy dtype support in affine helpers.
findings.status: open; fix outside review write scope
